uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort approximation from memory.

title: Use of administrative relationship data for secondary purposes
description: Names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationship information submitted for account administration could later be reused for analytics, profiling, messaging, or other purposes unrelated to account management without an appropriate legal basis or user expectation.
assumptions: The portal operator has technical ability to reuse submitted administration data outside the original purpose.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ; purpose-limitation/disclosure mapping is based on memory.

title: Linkability of family and role records across portal contexts
description: Parent-child links combined with names, emails, and roles can enable the portal to correlate records across student, parent, and administrator contexts, making it easier to connect actions and identities belonging to the same household or account network.
assumptions: The portal uses shared identifiers or common data stores across functions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree for linkability may be more specific.

title: Inference of sensitive family structure or custodial relationships
description: Even if only basic relationship links are entered, the portal may allow inference of sensitive facts such as guardianship patterns, non-traditional family structures, custody situations, or which adult is associated with which child.
assumptions: Relationship metadata and account states are visible to system operators or derivable from stored records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; inference-related subtree numbering may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of who created, changed, or disabled accounts and links
description: If the portal does not create trustworthy, tamper-resistant records of administrative actions, the school administrator could later deny having created, modified, or disabled an account or parent-child link, and affected users may be unable to prove what happened to their records.
assumptions: Administrative actions are security/privacy relevant and require auditability.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Administrator may be unaware of downstream handling of submitted personal data
description: The web app may not make it sufficiently clear how names, emails, roles, and relationship data will be stored, shared, retained, or used after submission. This can undermine transparency for the administrator acting on behalf of the school and for the data subjects affected.
assumptions: The portal UI/API does not fully explain processing, recipients, retention, or consequences of disabling/linking actions.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability/unawareness node id may differ.

title: Account and relationship management may not support privacy obligations
description: The portal may lack mechanisms needed to comply with privacy requirements when administering accounts and parent-child links, such as enforcing role-based restrictions, honoring correction/deletion requests, limiting retention after disablement, or maintaining lawful relationship records.
assumptions: Compliance obligations apply to student, parent, and staff account data handled by the portal.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id from memory; exact numbering may differ.

title: Linkability of student and parent accounts via stored relationship links
description: The account directory stores explicit parent-child relationship links alongside account records. An attacker or unauthorized internal user who can access directory contents may correlate multiple accounts and activities, linking a child account to one or more parent accounts and potentially linking siblings through shared guardians.
assumptions: The directory persists relationship identifiers or references that can be queried or inferred across records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability through stored relational identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Identifiability of students and guardians from account records
description: Writing account records into the directory may expose directly identifying attributes or stable account identifiers for students and parents/guardians. Even if names are partially hidden elsewhere, the directory can enable re-identification of individuals and households.
assumptions: Account records contain direct identifiers or unique persistent identifiers resolvable to real persons.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from stored identifying attributes.

title: Disclosure of family relationship data in the account directory
description: The flow writes sensitive relationship information to the directory, revealing which adult is linked to which child. Unauthorized access, overbroad internal access, or secondary use of the directory could disclose family structure, custody-related information, or educational associations.
assumptions: Relationship links are readable by components or staff beyond the minimum necessary set.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure from data at rest in a datastore.

title: Disclosure through excessive retention of historical relationship links
description: If the directory retains outdated account records or prior parent-child links after role changes, graduation, or custody updates, historical family associations may remain accessible and be disclosed beyond their valid purpose period.
assumptions: The datastore may retain superseded links or records without timely deletion.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture disclosure risk arising from retained historical data.

title: Unawareness of directory write and relationship propagation
description: Students and parents may be unaware that the grading service writes their account records and parent-child relationship links into a separate account directory, including who can access that directory and for what downstream purposes.
assumptions: Notice about this propagation and its recipients is incomplete, unclear, or not presented at the time data is collected or updated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient transparency about collection/use/disclosure across systems.

title: Non-compliance risk from storing relationship links without adequate purpose limitation or minimization
description: Persisting parent-child relationship links in the account directory may exceed what is necessary for account management if the same purpose could be achieved with less data or shorter retention. This creates risk of violating privacy requirements around data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or access control.
assumptions: Applicable policy or regulation requires minimization, limited retention, and restricted use of family relationship data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for non-compliance due to excessive collection/retention/use.

title: Excessive disclosure of student and staff data in full backup replication
description: The nightly replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third-party cloud hosting provider. This may disclose more personal data than is necessary for backup/hosting purposes, including sensitive educational records and directory information, to an external party.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is a separate controller/processor boundary and receives or can access the replicated backup contents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id is approximate; using a generic disclosure node because exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labels can vary by catalog version.

title: Unauthorized access to replicated backups at cloud provider
description: Once full backups are stored at the cloud hosting provider, provider personnel, compromised admin accounts, or co-tenant/cloud-side attackers could gain access to grade records, assignments, and account directory data, resulting in confidentiality loss.
assumptions: Backups are readable by the provider unless strong customer-managed encryption and access segregation are in place.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure via unauthorized access/storage exposure.

title: Linkability of academic, identity, and account datasets within replicated backups
description: The replicated dataset combines grade records, assignment submissions, and account directory information. At the cloud provider, these data categories can be linked together to build comprehensive profiles of individual students or staff across courses, performance, and identity records.
assumptions: The provider stores the replicated data in a form where records remain associated by account identifiers or other stable keys.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions; this is a best-fit generic linkability node.

title: Identifiability of individuals from full replicated records
description: Because the backup includes the account directory alongside grades and assignments, individuals are directly identifiable in the replicated data. Even if some application views are pseudonymous internally, the backup may preserve direct identifiers that reveal the identity of each data subject.
assumptions: Account directory contains names, emails, usernames, student/staff IDs, or equivalent direct identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Using a generic identifiability node as best fit; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Cross-border or secondary processing by cloud provider may violate purpose and transfer constraints
description: Sending full educational records and directory data to a third-party cloud provider may be incompatible with original collection purposes, contractual commitments, data residency requirements, or educational privacy obligations if the provider replicates, stores, or accesses the data in other jurisdictions or for operational purposes beyond backup/hosting.
assumptions: Applicable legal, contractual, or policy constraints limit third-party processing, onward transfer, or storage location of student records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node is approximate because exact LINDDUN Pro non-compliance subtree labels vary.

title: Backup replication may transmit unnecessary historical or deleted records
description: A full nightly backup can include stale, superseded, or deleted grade and assignment data that no longer need to be shared with the cloud provider, increasing disclosure risk and undermining storage limitation and minimization expectations.
assumptions: The backup process is full-image or broad-scope replication rather than filtered to only necessary operational data.
uncertainty_note: Approximate disclosure/minimization-related node selection.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their educational records are replicated to a third-party cloud host
description: Students and staff may not understand that their grades, assignments, and directory data are copied nightly to an external cloud hosting provider, reducing transparency about where their data are stored and who can access them.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product disclosures do not clearly explain third-party backup/hosting replication.
uncertainty_note: Using a generic unawareness node as best fit; exact numbering may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of grade records to the grading service
description: The data store may provide more grade-record attributes than are necessary for building a specific student, parent, or teacher view. Reading full grade records, including comments, historical grades, accommodations, or internal notes, can disclose personal data beyond the purpose of rendering the requested view.
assumptions: The service may query broad records and then filter in application logic rather than enforcing field-level minimization at the data-store interface.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for data minimization/excessive disclosure may differ.

title: Unauthorized role-based disclosure in generated views
description: Because the service builds views for students, parents, and teachers from the same grade records, it may expose data intended for one role to another role, such as teacher-only annotations appearing in a parent or student view.
assumptions: Different audiences have different authorization scopes over the same underlying grade records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for unauthorized disclosure/access-control-related disclosure.

title: Linkability of grade records across contexts and audiences
description: The service aggregates grade records to create multiple audience-specific views. If the same identifiers, record references, or stable metadata are reused across student, parent, and teacher interfaces, activities and records relating to the same student can be linked across contexts more easily than intended.
assumptions: Shared identifiers or consistent record structures are exposed across multiple views or logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro node for cross-context linkability may vary.

title: Inference of sensitive educational information from derived views
description: Even if direct fields are restricted, the service may derive or present aggregates, trends, missing-assignment indicators, or teacher feedback patterns that reveal sensitive information about student performance, learning difficulties, disciplinary issues, or accommodations.
assumptions: Views may include derived indicators or summaries, not just raw grades.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for indirect/derived disclosure; exact subtree may differ.

title: Use of grade records beyond the original purpose
description: Grade records stored for assessment and academic administration may be read by the service and repurposed broadly for multiple stakeholder views without clear purpose limitation, especially if additional analytics, ranking, or behavioral insights are generated during view construction.
assumptions: The implemented view-building may go beyond the purpose communicated at collection time or institutional policy.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact non-compliance subtree depends on the governing privacy requirements.

title: Insufficient transparency about grade-record access for view generation
description: Students and parents may be unaware that their grade records are being accessed from the database to generate different stakeholder views, what exact data elements are used, and which recipients can see them. This reduces predictability of processing.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate access patterns and audience-specific disclosures.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/unawareness; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Insufficient auditability of grade-record reads and disclosures
description: If reads from the grade database and subsequent disclosures into student, parent, and teacher views are not logged with sufficient detail, the organization may be unable to demonstrate who accessed which grade records for which audience, hindering accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: Audit trails for internal service reads and downstream view generation may be incomplete or not retained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation/accountability-related threat; exact subtree may differ.
